questions.problem:
Calculate $∇\cdot (\frac{1}{2}F)$ for the vector field $F$ where

$$
F=x{e}^{2x}\,i-y{e}^{2x}\,j+x{z}^{2}\,k.
$$
questions.worked_solution:
If $F$ and $G$ are vector fields and $k$ is a constant, then we have the following  linearity properties for divergence:

- $∇\cdot (kF)=k∇\cdot F$

- $∇\cdot (F+G)=∇\cdot F+∇\cdot G.$

In our case, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\cdot (\frac{1}{2}F)=\frac{1}{2}∇\cdot F.\end{aligned}
$$

First, we need to calculate $∇\cdot F.$ In doing so, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\cdot F & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(x{e}^{2x})+\frac{∂}{∂y}(-y{e}^{2x})+\frac{∂}{∂z}(x{z}^{2}) \\  & ={e}^{2x}+2x{e}^{2x}-{e}^{2x}+2xz \\  & =2x{e}^{2x}+2xz.\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the linearity properties, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\cdot (\frac{1}{2}F) & =\frac{1}{2}∇\cdot F \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot (2x{e}^{2x}+2xz) \\  & =x{e}^{2x}+xz.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Calculate $∇\cdot (3F+2G)$ for the vector fields $F$ and $G,$ where

$$
F={e}^{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}\,i+\operatorname{cos}⁡({y}^{2})\,j,\,∇\cdot G=3y\operatorname{sin}⁡({y}^{2}).
$$
questions.worked_solution:
If $F$ and $G$ are vector fields and $k$ is a constant, then we have the following  linearity properties for divergence:

- $∇\cdot (kF)=k∇\cdot F$

- $∇\cdot (F+G)=∇\cdot F+∇\cdot G.$

In our case, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\cdot (3F+2G) & =∇\cdot (3F)+∇\cdot (2G) \\  & =3∇\cdot F+2∇\cdot G.\end{aligned}
$$

First, we need to calculate $∇\cdot F.$ In doing so, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\cdot F & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({e}^{\operatorname{sin}⁡x})+\frac{∂}{∂y}(\operatorname{cos}⁡({y}^{2})) \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡x{e}^{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}-2y\operatorname{sin}⁡({y}^{2}).\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the linearity properties, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\cdot (3F+2G) & =3∇\cdot F+2∇\cdot G \\  & =3(\operatorname{cos}⁡x{e}^{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}-2y\operatorname{sin}⁡({y}^{2}))+2\cdot (3y\operatorname{sin}⁡({y}^{2})) \\  & =3\operatorname{cos}⁡x\,{e}^{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}-6y\operatorname{sin}⁡({y}^{2})+6y\operatorname{sin}⁡({y}^{2}) \\  & =3\operatorname{cos}⁡x\,{e}^{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}.\end{aligned}
$$

$$
∇\cdot (f\,F)=f\,∇\cdot F+F\cdot ∇f
$$

First, we compute $∇\cdot F$ and $∇f.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f & =⟨1,0⟩, \\ ∇\cdot F & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(y{e}^{-x})+\frac{∂}{∂y}(-y{e}^{y})=-y{e}^{-x}-{e}^{y}-y{e}^{y}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\cdot (f\,F) & =f\,∇\cdot F+F\cdot ∇f \\  & =x(-y{e}^{-x}-{e}^{y}-y{e}^{y})+⟨y{e}^{-x},-y{e}^{y}⟩\cdot ⟨1,0⟩ \\  & =-yx{e}^{-x}-x{e}^{y}-yx{e}^{y}+y{e}^{-x} \\  & =y{e}^{-x}-yx{e}^{-x}-x{e}^{y}-yx{e}^{y} \\  & =y(1-x){e}^{-x}-x(1+y){e}^{y}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Calculate $∇\cdot (-4F)$ for the vector field $F$ where

$$
F={x}^{2}yz\,i+({y}^{3}-y)\,j-xy{z}^{2}\,k.
$$
questions.worked_solution:
If $F$ and $G$ are vector fields and $k$ is a constant, then we have the following  linearity properties for divergence:

- $∇\cdot (kF)=k∇\cdot F$

- $∇\cdot (F+G)=∇\cdot F+∇\cdot G.$

In our case, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\cdot (-4F)=-4∇\cdot F.\end{aligned}
$$

First, we need to calculate $∇\cdot F.$ In doing so, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\cdot F & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}yz)+\frac{∂}{∂y}({y}^{3}-y)+\frac{∂}{∂z}(-xy{z}^{2}) \\  & =2xyz+3{y}^{2}-1-2xyz \\  & =3{y}^{2}-1.\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the linearity properties, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\cdot (-4F) & =-4∇\cdot F \\  & =-4\cdot (3{y}^{2}-1) \\  & =4-12{y}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
